newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa minerals bureau sees gold at $415 in 2001.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa minerals bureau sees gold at $415 in 2001.

text.p: The dollar gold price is expected to rise gradually to reach $415 an ounce by 2001, South Africa's Minerals Bureau said in its annual review.
The bureau, part of the department of mineral and energy affairs, said it expected gold to remain "weakly bullish" supported by physical demand exceeding supply.
"Worldwide physical gold demand is expected to remain buoyant in the medium term, supported in particular by Asian jewellery fabrication demand," the review said.
Gold was fixed on Tuesday in London at $357.65 -- its lowest level since October 1993 -- but dealers said the market was heavily oversold and predicted it would correct in the near term.
The bureau said it expected marginal increases in global gold output in the medium term.
"Marginal increases are expected over the more medium term, boosted by higher supplies from Australia and countries other than the top ten producers," the review said.
